description: Cross-layer onboarding preparation contract matrix (F6). One scenario describes one instant of one Agent setup world and carries: the selected Runtime identity, the local (CLI) facts and verdict an executing Agent consumes, independent Server observation facts with the canonical stage projection, a canonical exact-Agent snapshot fixture, and the Web presentation expectations. CLI, Server, and Web tests live in different packages and each consume only this file plus their own public boundary; nobody imports another package's internals.

presentationLimitations.description: The Server drops an expired readiness report at its TTL and exposes the leg as waiting with no old timestamp; an observation that never arrived is exposed identically. The Web cannot distinguish 'never arrived' from 'expired' and must not fabricate stale/expired evidence: both facts project to fail-closed waiting rows (never permanent checking, never a stale claim). This matrix records the limitation explicitly and pins the identical fail-closed projections from both server facts (scenarios no-fresh-observation and expired-observation); no schema extension is made to carry expiry client-side.
presentationLimitations.assertion: waiting, not checking; identical canonical snapshot from both facts

presentationLimitations.description: A CLI local result is local authority only. It never writes a Server stage, never claims Server readiness, and never reuses the consumed connect code. Messaging starts only when fresh daemon observations make the Server snapshot gate pass; scenarios no-fresh-observation and expired-observation carry localReady=true with a Server snapshot that is still gated.
presentationLimitations.assertion: connected=true plus exit code and guidance carry the local verdict; the Web gate stays closed until fresh reports

presentationLimitations.description: OpenTag never installs a Runtime CLI. A missing/login/config-failed Runtime always surfaces as an explicit human instruction plus an idempotent read-only runtime-inspect verify command, never as an install/repair command of its own.
presentationLimitations.assertion: instruction, never a Runtime repair command

presentationLimitations.description: checking is a real observation (a report or a cross-process ensure ownership), never a default: a missing or expired report is waiting. install is installation required, never a claim that installation is in progress.
